release_notes: The square-pixel rump mark reads as a C curl with a central void and inner return.
The foreleg mark reads as one tapered three-prong flame at thumbnail and full size.
The 0.1-unit fur-matched decal is visually flush with no plaque or silhouette artifact.
All reviewed limb, tail, and horn attachments remain continuous.

rectangular barrel, pillar forelegs, insufficient forward horn curl, and weak facial framing
visibly detached hind foot plus upright massing and generic rectangular markings

blind_failure_history.reason: raised cream pieces read as plaques and staples rather than fur markings
UV resampling and occlusion reduced the spiral to chevrons and the flames to forked runes

visual_review: The v8 candidate is a true native quadruped volume with no image-depth walls, contour panels, or photographic skin cuboids.
A short rising trunk and high wide shoulder replace the level barrel and diminish the connected crouched rump.
The front limbs use three connected pitched volumes plus compact pads, while the narrower rear chains visibly overlap their paws.
Twenty-two overlapping mane and beard volumes frame the crown, cheeks, shoulders, chest, and jaw.
Each horn projects outward and forward around the face, with a thick base, broad open curl, narrowing return, and upturned pale tip.
The identity marks use opaque embedded pixel art on existing or fur-matched flush surfaces instead of raised color-only geometry.
limitations: Far-side markings are conservative inferences from one three-quarter reference.
Curves and flame shapes remain intentionally Minecraft-native stepped abstractions.
Uniform alignment compensates only scale and translation; silhouette scores are evaluation evidence, not construction inputs.
The source page offers only a proprietary non-commercial .max file, so it was not represented as usable GLB input.
The generic mesh route emits a static one-bone model; semantic rigging remains a separate reviewed pass.
Final cumulative pass/fail remains reserved for the independent cumulative grader.
